paragraphs: Friend, this passage is a warning label on hatred left alone. Absalom said nothing to Amnon for two years after what happened to Tamar, and the quiet fooled everybody (2 Samuel 13:22). It wasn't peace. Hatred that nobody deals with doesn't leave, it just waits for a day with a good guest list.

Look at what the text lets us see. Absalom's plan is dressed up as a party, and Jonadab says Absalom has planned this since the day Amnon violated Tamar (2 Samuel 13:32). One sin lit a fire, and a second sin, a killing, walked right through the same door. I think that's the heavy part, because everybody in this family is hurting, and nobody in the passage turns toward God with it. Hurt doesn't fix itself when we take matters into our own hands. It just spreads to more people.

And look where it leaves David: weeping, mourning every day, and a son gone to Geshur for three years (2 Samuel 13:36-38). Then the text says David longed to go to Absalom (2 Samuel 13:39). So here's the takeaway, baker. Bring your hurt to God and to people who can help before it grows teeth, because the longer it sits, the more it costs. This family's story isn't over, and neither is the lesson.
